audit_findings.title: The anchor may normalize away core working-capital reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $935.4 million combined filed impacts ($507.3 million receivables plus $428.1 million inventories); $563.6 million OE-minus-OCF gap, equal to 81.8% of the $688.6 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A recurring receivables-and-inventory cash charge would reduce owner earnings and the cash-supported growth rate throughout the forecast and terminal period.
audit_findings.evidence: The $976.2 million decrease is primarily driven by a $507.3 million impact from changes in trade accounts receivable and a $428.1 million impact from changes in inventories.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash consumption is demonstrated, but whether it is temporary or recurring is unresolved. Its scale relative to the anchor is large enough that treating project-related working capital as fully reversible while forecasting growth could materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every FY2025 working-capital normalization in the OE calculation, calculate historical working capital required per dollar of organic growth by segment, and rerun all scenarios with recurring receivables and inventory investment tied to projected growth.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized cloud spending may evade the maintenance-capex deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.2 million FY2025 amortization; gross capitalized implementation costs increased $85.6 million from $257.8 million to $343.4 million, while net carrying value increased $55.4 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back cloud amortization without deducting capitalized implementation cash spending inflates owner earnings; omitting sustainable replacement spending also inflates terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Capitalized implementation costs, which are recorded as a component of other assets in the Consolidated Balance Sheets, were $ 343.4 million and $ 257.8 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and the related accumulated amortization was $ 59.8 million and $ 29.6 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed balances demonstrate economically capitalized technology investment, but the supplied record does not establish how the OE calculation treated its amortization or cash additions. The $85.6 million gross balance increase equals 12.4% of the anchor, so the possible omission is reasonably capable of materially affecting value.
audit_findings.action: Trace cloud amortization and implementation payments through the OE bridge, identify FY2025 cash additions rather than relying only on balance changes, and rerun the valuation with amortization left expensed or with recurring cloud maintenance spending deducted.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 straddles a preferred-to-debt refinancing and may mix claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $32.9 million redemption gain, $27.3 million preferred dividends, and $51.0 million computed annual coupon on $800 million of 6.375% notes; net anchor effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The common-equity OE numerator must exclude the non-operating redemption gain, remove only the obsolete preferred dividend burden, and include the continuing after-tax interest burden associated with the replacement debt.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recognized a $ 32.9 million gain from the redemption as income attributable to common stockholders.
audit_findings.explanation: The transitional items and their amounts are demonstrated, but the supplied OE bridge does not show their actual treatment. The gain and preferred dividends substantially offset, while only part of the annual note interest was absent from FY2025, so the record cannot establish the net valuation effect or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Produce the line-by-line reconciliation from GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders to $688.6 million OE, then rerun after removing the gain, adding back only the obsolete preferred dividends, and annualizing after-tax interest on the 2033 Notes.

audit_findings.title: Uncertain-tax liabilities may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $164.7 million, equal to $3.31 per diluted share and 1.6% of the $10,484 million base equity value if the entire amount were deducted dollar-for-dollar
audit_findings.mechanism: Any portion not already represented in normalized tax expense would enter as a finite senior claim against equity or as future cash tax payments reducing OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Liabilities related to unrecognized tax benefits, including interest and penalties, of $164.7 million were excluded from the table above as we cannot reasonably estimate the timing of these potential cash settlements with taxing authorities.
audit_findings.explanation: Treatment remains worth confirming, but even the conservative assumption that the entire filed liability is incremental reduces base value from $210.39 to approximately $207.08 per share. That scale does not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $351.46 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $164.7 million liability to taxes and related interest already recognized in the OE series; deduct only any residual amount not represented, with no probability-weighting unless supported by filed evidence.

audit_findings.title: Retained interest expense may not represent future borrowing costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.5 million annual pretax interest change per 100 basis points, equal to 2.8% of the anchor; the completed 2026 fixed-note refinancing computes to $15.2 million lower annual coupon before use-of-proceeds effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level DCF, changes in variable rates and refinancing coupons flow through retained interest expense and therefore change future OE without a separate debt-principal deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: A 100 basis point rise or decline in interest rates would result in an increase or decrease to interest expense of $19.5 million under our current capital structure.
audit_findings.explanation: No anchor error is demonstrated. Rate movements remain forward-looking, and the cited 2028 refinancing has already occurred: $1.325 billion at 7.25% was replaced by $650 million at 5.25% and $850 million at 5.50%. The new fixed coupons lower annual interest on those notes, while higher principal and variable-rate exposure make the total direction mixed.
audit_findings.action: Update the prospective interest schedule for the completed refinancing and monitor actual variable balances; rerun rate sensitivities in 100-basis-point increments without deducting ordinary debt principal.

audit_findings.title: The cash addition may include amounts unavailable to common owners
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.6 million restricted at December 2025; June 2026 balance-sheet cash of $808.9 million versus $302.0 million included in company-defined available cash, a $506.9 million difference; unavailable portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted, operationally required, or tax-encumbered cash should be excluded from the equity bridge or reduced by the associated access cost.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash and cash equivalents in the Consolidated Balance Sheets include $ 16.6 million and $ 19.7 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, that is restricted from use to fund operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The record demonstrates that some cash was restricted at year-end and that the company counted substantially less than total June cash as available liquidity. It does not establish that the $506.9 million difference is unavailable to owners or quantify minimum operating cash, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 cash schedule by restriction, entity, jurisdiction, and operating requirement; reconcile it to the $302.0 million liquidity amount and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash net of filed repatriation taxes.
